newsitem.title: SAUDI ARABIA: Moslems celebrate end of tragic haj.
newsitem.headline: Moslems celebrate end of tragic haj.

text.p: Huge crowds of Moslems performed Eid al-Adha prayers at the Grand Mosque in Mecca early on Thursday marking the end of a tragic haj pilgrimage.

The Eid sermon made no mention of Tuesday's fire that tore through 70,000 tents at the plain of Mena, about 11 km (seven miles) from the Islamic holy city of Mecca, killing 343 people and injuring some 1,300.

At the prayers thousands of worshippers circling the cube-shaped Kaaba at the centre of the Grand Mosque, one of Islam's holiest shrines, were told by the mosque's imam that unity is essential to overcome attempts to weaken Islamic states and control their resources.
The imam accused Israel of trying to seize holy Arab land and kill innocent civilians.

At dawn, pilgrims in seamless white robes hurled stones at a pillar symbolising the devil on the outskirts of Mecca -- the last ritual of haj which reached its climax on Wednesday at Mount Arafat where the Prophet Mohammad gave his last sermon 14 centuries ago.
Pilgrims will slaughter hundreds of thousands of sheep and cattle to celebrate Eid al-Adha (the Feast of Sacrifice), which is celebrated by some one billion Moslems worldwide.

Saudi television on Wednesday showed many fire victims, some in critical condition, in hospital beds. Official Saudi media did not give the nationalities but diplomats said most of the dead were Indians, Pakistanis and Bangladeshis.
